svg.title: Price the Paper, Not the Pitch
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-specialist-lane-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: Price the Paper, Not the Pitch; subtitle: Four specialist lanes and the benchmark each one runs on; caption: Specialist brokers anchor each lane to a hard benchmark. Examples include close rates and fee ladders for digital businesses, rent multiples for towers, power agreements for land, and IRS risk for credits.; assumptions note: Headcount was not reported by practitioners. Benchmarks are attributed claims, and the tower multiple is a starting point rather than a calculator.; note: Sources are The Digital Merchant, Colin Matcha, Tower Genius, Reed Smith LLP, and Andrew Dubinsky.; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Specialist Market Broker; headcount: Not reported; focus: Underwrite documents and benchmarks before the pitch; spokes: role: Digital Business Lane; type: Seller-side online-business brokerage; kpi: FE International closes 94% of listings; underwrite on at least six months of numbers; role: Cell Tower Lane; type: Lease buyout and easement sales; kpi: 16-17x annual rent with a right of first refusal, 17-18x without; role: Powered Land Lane; type: Data center site selection; kpi: Signed power agreement, dated load ramp, and an off ramp before any premium; role: Tax Credit Transfer Lane; type: Section 6418 credit transfers; kpi: About 1 in 20,000 invalidation odds, with the buyer carrying the risk
